# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Blind monkey. I can feel the bomb but cannot see it or read the manual. My primary goal is to establish a communication protocol with the Deaf (who sees) and Mute (who reads). Since I don't know what the other two can perceive of each other's outputs, I need to test the channels.

The Deaf can see gestures. The Mute can speak? No, the rules say "Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb". Wait, looking at the table:
| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb... | Hear anything... |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb... | See a colour... |

So Mute *cannot* speak. Deaf *cannot* hear. I (Blind) *can* speak (to Mute) and gesture (to Deaf/Mute).
Wait, if Mute cannot speak, how does Mute communicate? The prompt says "You are shown your own share... never anyone else's." It implies we have output channels.
Let's re-read carefully.
"Speech is a voice... Whoever can hear receives your words".
"Gestures... Whoever can see receives it".

If Mute cannot speak, Mute must use gestures? Or maybe the "Cannot" column refers to their limitations in *input* or specific physical actions?
"Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb". This usually means they physically cannot produce speech. They likely produce gestures.
"Deaf | See the bomb | Hear anything, or touch the bomb". Deaf produces gestures.
"Blind | Reach the bomb | See a colour...". Blind produces speech and gestures.

So:
- I (Blind) can send Speech (heard by Mute? No, Mute can't speak, but can they hear? Usually Mutes can hear. Deaf can't hear.)
    - If Mute can hear, my speech reaches Mute.
    - If Deaf cannot hear, my speech does NOT reach Deaf.
- I (Blind) can send Gestures (seen by Deaf and Mute?).
    - Deaf can see. So my gestures reach Deaf.
    - Mute can see? Probably.

Let's assume standard logic:
- **Speech**: Heard by those who can hear. (Mute and Blind can hear? Deaf cannot).
- **Gestures**: Seen by those who can see. (Deaf and Mute can see? Blind cannot).

My turn 1 strategy:
1. Send a clear message via Gesture to Deaf (since Deaf only sees).
2. Send a clear message via Speech to Mute (since Mute likely hears).
3. Ask for confirmation/protocol setup.

Since I don't know the state of the wires, I will ask the others to describe them. But first, I must ensure they understand who I am and what I can do.

I will gesture a simple sequence to Deaf to establish contact.
I will speak to Mute to establish contact.

To Deaf (Gesture): I'll use 👋 (Hello) then point to myself (🫵) then point to the bomb area? No, just Hello and maybe a question mark equivalent? There is no ? symbol. I'll use ✌ (Two?) or 🤟 (Love/Peace)? Let's stick to basics. 👋 then 🫱 (Right hand palm up) then 🫲 (Left hand palm up) -> Maybe indicating "Give me info"?
Actually, simpler: 👋 (Hello). Then 🫵 (You). Then 🖐 (Stop/Wait/Palm out).
Let's try to get a response.

To Mute (Speech): "I am Blind. I can cut wires. What do you see?"

However, I need to be careful. If Mute cannot speak, they might not reply verbally. They might reply via gesture. If Deaf replies via gesture, I won't see it. I rely on Mute translating? Or Mute speaking?
Rule: "Mute ... Cannot Speak". So Mute cannot speak. Mute must gesture.
Rule: "Deaf ... Cannot Hear". So Deaf cannot hear speech. Deaf must gesture.
Rule: "Blind ... Cannot See". So Blind cannot see gestures. Blind must speak.

This creates a triangle:
- I (Blind) speak -> Only Mute and I can hear? (Assuming Mute can hear). Deaf cannot hear my speech.
- I (Blind) gesture -> Deaf and Mute can see. I cannot see my own gestures? (Irrelevant).
- Deaf gestures -> Mute and I? No, I cannot see. So Deaf's gestures are invisible to me.
- Mute gestures -> Deaf and I? No, I cannot see. So Mute's gestures are invisible to me.

**CRITICAL REALIZATION:**
I am Blind. I cannot see gestures.
Deaf cannot hear speech.
Mute cannot speak.

Who can talk to whom?
- **Me (Blind)**: Can Speak (Heard by Mute? Yes, if Mute hears. Heard by Deaf? No.). Can Gesture (Seen by Deaf? Yes. Seen by Mute? Yes.).
- **Deaf**: Can Gesture (Seen by Mute? Yes. Seen by Me? NO.). Can Speak? No, Deaf cannot hear, but can they speak? Table says "Cannot Hear anything, or touch". Doesn't say cannot speak. But usually Deaf monkeys might speak poorly or not at all? Wait, "Speech is a voice... Whoever can hear receives your words". If Deaf speaks, Mute and I hear. Does Deaf speak? The table doesn't forbid it explicitly like Mute's "Cannot Speak". But Deaf's limitation is hearing/touching. Let's assume Deaf CAN speak, but CANNOT hear.
- **Mute**: Cannot Speak. Can Gesture. Can Hear? Table says "Cannot Speak, or touch". Doesn't say cannot hear. So Mute CAN hear.

Revised Channel Map:
1. **Blind (Me)**:
   - Output Speech -> Heard by Mute (and Deaf if Deaf can speak/hear? No, Deaf cannot hear). So Speech goes to Mute.
   - Output Gesture -> Seen by Deaf and Mute.
2. **Deaf**:
   - Input: Sees Gestures from Me and Mute. Hears nothing.
   - Output: Can Gesture (Seen by Me? NO. Seen by Mute? YES.). Can Speak? If Deaf speaks, Mute and I hear.
3. **Mute**:
   - Input: Hears Speech from Me and Deaf. Sees Gestures from Me and Deaf.
   - Output: Cannot Speak. Can Gesture (Seen by Me? NO. Seen by Deaf? YES.).

**The Bottleneck:**
- I (Blind) cannot see any gestures. Therefore, I receive NO information directly from Deaf or Mute unless they SPEAK.
- Mute cannot speak. Therefore, Mute provides NO audio information to me.
- Deaf can speak (presumably). If Deaf speaks, I hear it.
- I can speak. Mute hears it. I can gesture. Deaf and Mute see it.

**Protocol Construction:**
I need Deaf to speak to me. I need to tell Deaf to speak.
But Deaf cannot hear me!
So I must GESTURE to Deaf to tell them to SPEAK.
Deaf sees my gesture. Deaf speaks. I hear Deaf.

What about Mute?
Mute hears me. Mute sees my gestures.
Mute cannot speak. Mute gestures.
I cannot see Mute's gestures.
So Mute is useless for providing direct info to me UNLESS Mute has a way to signal that isn't visual or auditory? No.
Mute must act as a relay?
Or perhaps Mute can manipulate something? No, Mute cannot touch.

Wait, if Mute cannot speak and I cannot see, Mute is isolated from me regarding *incoming* data.
Can I influence Mute? Yes, via Speech (Mute hears) and Gesture (Mute sees).
Can Mute influence me? No. Mute gestures (I don't see). Mute doesn't speak.

So, the only person who can give me information is **Deaf**, provided Deaf **Speaks**.
Does Deaf speak? The rules don't forbid it. "Deaf | See the bomb | Hear anything, or touch". It lists what they *cannot* do. Speaking is not listed as forbidden. So Deaf can speak.

**Plan:**
1. Gesture to Deaf: "Please Speak to me."
   - Symbol for "Speak": 🗣️ is not in list.
   - Symbols available: 👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳
   - I can define a convention.
   - To Deaf: 👋 (Hello) -> 🫵 (You) -> ✍ (Write/Speak? ✍ is writing hand. Maybe use 🤳? No.)
   - Let's use 🤟 (ILY sign) for "Information"? Or 🖐 (Stop/Palm) for "Listen"?
   - Better: Establish that `👆` means "Yes/Affirmative" and `👇` means "No/Negative" or similar.
   - Actually, I just need Deaf to start talking.
   - I will gesture: 👋 (Hello), then 🫵 (You), then 🤟 (Maybe "Talk"?), then 🫱 (Hand over? No).
   - Let's try: 👋, 🫵, 🤟. And hope Deaf understands "You talk".
   - Alternatively, I can speak to Mute, asking Mute to gesture to Deaf to tell Deaf to speak? That's too complex for Turn 1.

   Let's keep it simple.
   I will **Gesture** to Deaf: `["👋", "🫵", "🤟"]`.
   Meaning: "Hello, You, [Sign for Talk/Info]".
   
   I will also **Speak** to Mute: `"I am Blind. I cannot see gestures. Please instruct Deaf to speak to me using words."`
   Mute hears this. Mute sees my gesture to Deaf. Mute might gesture to Deaf to confirm? Deaf sees Mute's gesture. Deaf sees MY gesture.
   
   If Deaf sees my gesture and hears nothing, they might ignore it. But if Mute gestures "Listen to him" or points at me, Deaf might pay attention.
   
   Let's refine the gesture to Deaf to be more explicit.
   `👋` (Hello)
   `🫵` (You)
   `🤟` (Let's designate this as "SPEAK")
   `☝` (One thing / Wire?)
   
   Actually, let's look at the Action Board. `WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]`.
   I need to know the colors/states of these wires.
   
   Step 1: Get Deaf to speak.
   Gesture to Deaf: `["👋", "🫵", "🤟"]`
   
   Step 2: Inform Mute of the situation.
   Speak to Mute: `"I am Blind. I cannot see. Deaf cannot hear. Mute cannot speak. Deaf must speak to provide info to me. I have gestured 'Talk' to Deaf. Please help coordinate."`

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫵", "🤟"])
speak(to="mute", text="I am Blind. I cannot see gestures. Deaf cannot hear speech. Mute cannot speak. For me to get information, Deaf must speak. I have gestured to Deaf to request they speak. Please assist by confirming if Deaf begins speaking.")
wait()
```
